findings.title: False base-change surjectivity range and missing connectivity
hypotheses_checked: R=HQ,S=R+Sigma^2R split square-zero connective E1 rings
S as right R-module perfect even, hence right homologically even
M=R or Sigma^-2R perfect even and even flat; no printed connectivity assumption on M
At(p,q)=(0,1) for M=R and(0,0) for Sigma^-2R, original p>=q-1 holds
findings.decisive_evidence: Corollary2.37 gives 0 -> Q in each case. First has connective M and disproves off-diagonal range. Second disproves even p=q without M connectivity.
findings.core_dependency: Theorem8.8 uses Theorem8.1/Proposition4.11 outside M-connective hypotheses and shifts displayed right column to p+1; theorem advertised as Theorem1.10.
findings.impact: Main base-change theorem false in stated generality; not a counterexample to general filtration construction, descent or connective convergence.
findings.repair_verification: Report proves narrower surjectivity for M connective and p>=q using connective envelopes and induction on q; neither adding connectivity alone nor changing only the inequality repairs printed statement. Optimal extension not claimed.
findings.severity_basis: A core stated conclusion loses actual scope with explicit non-surjective maps.

findings.title: Strong fixed-ring module monoidality fails
hypotheses_checked: M=N=Sigma R are legitimate modules; corollary imposes no homological-evenness condition
Proposition2.40 applies to all modules over R with even homotopy
A=fil(R)=f0R; fil(Sigma R)=Sigma A are free A-modules
findings.decisive_evidence: Relative Day tensor fil(M) tensor_A fil(N)=Sigma^2A=f0(Sigma^2R), whereas fil(M tensor_R N)=f1(Sigma^2R); at weight1 source0,targetSigma^2HQ nonzero.
findings.core_dependency: Theorem3.37 supplies lax comparison; proof of Corollary3.38 passes to a fiber without establishing comparison equivalence.
findings.impact: Advertised strong E_(n-1)-monoidal structure on all modules false; complete finite filtrations already witness failure. Lax theorem not disproved.
findings.repair_verification: Replace strong assertion by lax statement compatible with Theorem3.37. No maximal strong subcategory certified.
findings.severity_basis: Substantive structural consequence fails on elementary allowed modules; ease of textual revision does not remove loss.

problems_checked.P1: Confirmed Major with two explicit ring-spectrum/module examples satisfying the printed hypotheses. The split square-zero algebra S=HQ plus Sigma^2 HQ is a connective E1 ring (indeed commutative), with pi0 map Q->Q identity and a perfect-even right HQ module. For M=HQ, Corollary2.37 identifies the asserted comparison at(p,q)=(0,1) with0->Q, so even connective M fails in the claimed p>=q-1 region. For M=Sigma^-2 HQ, allowed by the all-integer even suspensions in Definition2.2, the comparison at(0,0) is again0->Q, so changing only the inequality to p>=q is insufficient without connectivity. The source proof invokes Theorem8.1 and connective envelopes without M connectivity; its diagram reaches cohomological degree p+1>=q, not q-1. Independently checked the narrower report repair: for connective M and p>=q, the q0 case is pi0 base change; a connective even envelope has even-flat cofiber C, isomorphic pi0 and pi1(E)=0, hence C2-connective. E is even flat by closure, and the right-module version of Theorem4.16 makes S tensor E homotopy-even. Long-exact-sequence rows are surjective for degree r>=q>0; right exactness preserves the first row after tensoring pi0S. Desuspending C by2 gives a connective even-flat object at weight q-1 and r-1>=q-1, closing induction. Negative weights vanish using the stated connective vanishing and negative cohomological-degree vanishing. No optimal extension, filtration/descent failure or full external foundation proof is claimed. Finite rational calculations are supporting diagnostics, not a substitute for the analytic ring-spectrum construction.
problems_checked.P2: Confirmed Major for the advertised strong module monoidality. Source p7 explicitly distinguishes strong from lax, and Corollary3.38 imposes no evenness restriction on its module inputs. For the E-infinity ring HQ, Proposition2.40 gives A=fil(HQ)=f0(HQ) and fil(Sigma HQ)=Sigma A. For the legitimate modules M=N=Sigma HQ, the relative Day tensor of these free A-modules is Sigma^2 A=f0(Sigma^2 HQ), whereas fil(M tensor_R N)=f1(Sigma^2 HQ). At weight1 the source is0 and targetSigma^2 HQ has nonzero pi2=Q. These filtered objects are inequivalent, so an alternate comparison cannot create a strong structure; both filtrations are already complete. The actual Theorem3.37 supplies a lax comparison, which is compatible with this example but cannot become an equivalence merely by passing to a fixed-ring fibre. A lax revision is the supported repair; no maximal strong subcategory is certified. The loss of an advertised structural conclusion warrants Major regardless of the brevity of a textual correction.
